g.ns45:text: Accelerating Loops with Arrays
Florian Frohn and J\xfcrgen Giesl
IJCAR 2026
\\color{red} Displacing!
Horn Clauses (SMT-LIB)

$\\exists n \\in \\mathbb{N}.\\ \\underbrace{i + n \\leq k}_{\\mathclap{\\substack{\\text{Runtime $\\geq n$}\\\\\\text{Acceleration Calculus}}}} = k' \\land \\underbrace{i' = i + n}_{\\mathclap{\\substack{\\text{Closed Form}\\\\\\text{Recurrence Solving}}}}$
\\color{red} Inductive!
can be eliminated if $i$ changes by a \\textbf{constant}
can be replaced by $\\lambda$
$a' = \\lambda j.\\ \\textbf{if}\\ (0 \\leq j < n + i)\\ a[j+1]\\ \\textbf{elif}\\ (1 \\leq j = n + i)\\ a[i]\\ \\textbf{else}\\ a[j]$

\\[\n\\forall \\underbrace{j \\in \\mathbb{N}}_{\\mathclap{\\text{array index}}}, \\overbrace{k \\in [0,n-1]}^{\\mathclap{\\text{iteration counter}}}.\\ \\underbrace{j = i^{(k)} + 1}_{\\mathclap{\\substack{\\text{$a[j]$ is written}\\\\\\text{by $a[i+1] \\gets a[i]$}\\\\\\text{in the $k^{th}$ iteration}}}} \\implies \\overbrace{a'[j] = a[i]^{(k)}}^{\\mathclap{\\substack{\\text{final value of $a[j]$}\\\\\\text{is equal to value of $a[i]$}\\\\\\text{in the $k^{th}$ iteration}}}} \\land \\ldots\n\\]
\\begin{theorem}\nArray-Solvable loops\\\\admit closed forms for lvalues.\n\\end{theorem}
It works!

Does that work for anything but $\\mathbb{Z}$?
Can you handle other theories?
\\color{blue} Yes!
